name: The Stone Tally
story: The scale keeper counts what the bones are owed, and the tally is heavier than the tomb.

beforeStory.speaker: The Long Road
beforeStory.text: Tally stones hang in a net above the scale. The keeper moves one for Arith before either of them speaks.

beforeStory.speaker: Scale Keeper
beforeStory.text: The bones lent out a whole war and asked to be paid back. I am still counting the interest.

beforeStory.speaker: The Long Road
beforeStory.text: Arith sets his hand on the empty pan. The net does not sway, so the keeper adds another stone.

afterStory.speaker: The Long Road
afterStory.text: The keeper chalks a figure on the wall, wipes it with his sleeve, and chalks it again.

afterStory.speaker: Scale Keeper
afterStory.text: Leave the stones where they are. I have not finished the sum, and I do not want to start it again.

name: What the Bones Counted
story: The accounting room asks Arith to add without any of the crown's tricks.

beforeStory.speaker: The Long Road
beforeStory.text: The accounting room is chalked from the door to the far wall. Cinder lamps stand at the corners with numbers written on their shades.

beforeStory.speaker: Scale Keeper
beforeStory.text: No crown arithmetic and nothing borrowed. Add the columns and the floor opens on the next room.

beforeStory.speaker: The Long Road
beforeStory.text: Arith kneels and counts on his fingers. A cinder steps off its mark to watch.

afterStory.speaker: The Long Road
afterStory.text: The floor opens on a stair with one lamp at the bottom. Chalk is still on Arith's palm.

afterStory.speaker: Scale Keeper
afterStory.text: The total was off by one and the floor opened anyway. Do not tell the next one that it worked.

name: The Keeper's Refusal
story: The keeper will not teach the stone's lesson while anyone is watching, and he wants it to hurt.

beforeStory.speaker: The Long Road
beforeStory.text: The keeper puts out the lamp and sends the last cinder out through the low door. One stone in his hand lights the room.

beforeStory.speaker: Keeper
beforeStory.text: Nobody watching and nobody helping. That is the lesson, and I want it to cost you something.

beforeStory.speaker: The Long Road
beforeStory.text: Arith puts his back to the wall and lifts his hands. The keeper does not offer to hold the stone for him.

afterStory.speaker: The Long Road
afterStory.text: Arith's hands are raw where the stone turned in them. The keeper sets it on the floor between them and steps back.

afterStory.speaker: Keeper
afterStory.text: It is yours now. Do not thank me. Ask for it again when it stops being enough.

chapter: Chapter III - The Queue at the Gate
name: No Replacement Appointed
story: The tomb's gate keeper finally has relief, and the relief cannot get past the queue.

beforeStory.speaker: The Long Road
beforeStory.text: A guard sits on the gate step with his helmet in his lap. The queue behind him has not moved all afternoon.

beforeStory.speaker: Relieved Guard
beforeStory.text: My relief is in that line. He has been in it since noon.

beforeStory.speaker: The Long Road
beforeStory.text: Arith takes off his pack and stands at the end of the queue. The people ahead of him make room without turning around.

afterStory.speaker: The Long Road
afterStory.text: The relief reaches the step after dark and holds out a wooden token. The guard gives him the helmet and does not ask for it back.

afterStory.speaker: Relieved Guard
afterStory.text: I am going home. If the queue asks for me, tell it I am still here.

chapter: Chapter III - The Queue at the Gate
name: The Long Watch
story: One night standing at the gate, and the gate is not empty at night.

beforeStory.speaker: The Long Road
beforeStory.text: The keeper hands Arith a lantern and a stick of chalk. The gate goes dark from the top down.

beforeStory.speaker: Watch
beforeStory.text: Count them as they come. Every name you chalk gets a place inside in the morning.

beforeStory.speaker: The Long Road
beforeStory.text: Arith chalks the first name. The wind takes the dust off the stone and he writes it again.

afterStory.speaker: The Long Road
afterStory.text: By dawn the gate is chalked from the threshold to the hinge. The bandage at Arith's side has gone dark, and he keeps writing.

afterStory.speaker: Watch
afterStory.text: Whoever you left off the list will come back tonight. Leave the chalk where it lies.

chapter: Chapter III - The Queue at the Gate
name: A Place at the Gate
story: The keeper can leave the gate, but only if someone beats the captain's terms.

beforeStory.speaker: The Long Road
beforeStory.text: The gate captain sets three terms on the step: the gate, the queue, and the road behind it. The keeper stands where he was posted.

beforeStory.speaker: Gate Captain
beforeStory.text: Leave your post and the gate shuts behind you. That is the first term, and the other two are worse.

beforeStory.speaker: The Long Road
beforeStory.text: Arith puts his hand on the gate chain and waits. The keeper does not ask him to stop.

afterStory.speaker: The Long Road
afterStory.text: The chain comes down. Bram steps over the line he has kept for forty years and leaves his staff against the gate.

afterStory.speaker: Bram
afterStory.text: Forty years I had a post and no reason to leave it. May I walk with you as far as the road goes?
